flawed_step: Lines 51 and 63 assert that five colors guarantee an available non-conflicting color for any next vertex, regardless of prior legal color choices. The five-color theorem does not imply this extension property for partial colorings.
counterexample: Let the planar graph be the star K_{1,5}, with center u and leaves a,b,c,d,e. Select and legally color the pairwise nonadjacent leaves red, green, blue, yellow, and black, respectively. When u is selected, every available color occurs on one of its neighbors, so no legal color exists. The graph has no triangles, so the triangle argument in lines 55–63 does not address this obstruction.
assessment_summary: This explicit legal partial coloring refutes the proof's key universal availability claim. The proof does not establish that its proposed vertex-selection rule prevents such an obstruction, so its conclusion does not follow.
